claim: Seeding the autoconvolution with a power-law profile h_i ∝ (i+0.5)^-1/2 and then hill-climbing in log-height space reaches R≈0.88, far above the 2/3 constant seed; the seed's f*f is nearly flat over half the support, so the plateau is already near-optimal before local search.

Plain multi-resolution stochastic hill climb from the constant start (no power-law prior) reaches R≈0.81, showing the seed matters: the same optimizer family gains ~0.14 from the constant start but ~0.21 from the power-law seed.

claim: Raising resolution from N=2000 to N=20000 with the same power-law seed and optimizer gives only a marginal gain (0.8779 → 0.8808), so resolution is not the binding constraint; the plateau shape, not the grid, sets the ceiling near 0.88.

Wide-loop multi-start searches from the constant start reached only 0.75–0.78 (p0005, p0006), below the deep coarse-to-fine run (0.81); whether the gap is due to search strategy or budget allocation is unresolved, and p0002 returned its start unchanged after 27 s so its idea is untested.

Scanning genuinely different seed families (two-sided power law, spike+bang-bang, edge-spike) at coarse N and then climbing does not escape the power-law basin: the best of the family scan plus short climbs, upsampled and continued, lands at 0.880786, only +0.000002 over the power-law start. Quasi-Newton (L-BFGS-B with finite-difference gradients) ascent in log-height at coarse resolutions, upsampled and finished with the block climber, gains only +0.000001 over the power-law start (0.880785). Gradient information does not find a better shape than random block moves on this plateau; the optimum is not a gradient-limited one.

Perturb-and-restart from the best construction plus adaptive coordinate hill climb gives the largest gain of the generation, +0.000082 (0.880784 → 0.880865), by nudging the plateau slightly flatter (f*f within 0.1% of max rises 30.83%→30.85%). The improvement is real but tiny, confirming the plateau shape is near-saturated for this construction.

claim: A deterministic multiscale block-scaling sweep with FFT scoring returned its start unchanged after 28 s of a 30 s budget, so it is untested rather than failed; it needs a longer budget or a cheaper schedule to show whether systematic block sweeps beat random block moves.

Exact-gradient L-BFGS-B ascent in log-height using a smooth p-norm max (p=8..64) at N=20000 gains only +0.000003 over the power-law start (0.880865 → 0.880868), so coherent whole-plateau gradient reshaping does not beat coordinate hill climb at this resolution; the plateau is already near a local optimum for this objective and the binding constraint is discretization, not the optimizer.

A systematic multiplicative log-tilt and right-edge mass-boost grid over the N=20000 construction gains only +0.000001 (0.880865 → 0.880866), so the global mass balance between the left singularity and the second-half tail is already essentially optimal; local search has not missed a better global tilt.

tag: tail-envelope optimization on high-n binomial seed
claim: Multiplicative power-law envelopes on the last 40% of the N=200000 binomial seed, optimized by coordinate descent on 8 coefficients plus local log-polish, leave the score unchanged at 0.882542 (p0020). Reshaping the right edge multiplicatively does not steepen the f*f tail enough to raise R, so the tail mass is not reachable by smooth envelope modulation of the seed's right end.

Forcing the binomial seed to taper to zero over its last part (power taper from a breakpoint K, grid over K and exponent s, then coordinate refine and a 5-coef tail envelope) never beats the pure binomial: score stays 0.882542 (p0025). Cutting the tail products by truncating h's right end does not raise R, so the plateau loss is not recovered by a forced decay edge.

Single-mode and paired low-frequency modulations of the binomial seed (cosine modes m=1..4, several amplitudes, then coordinate refine) do not beat the start by more than 1e-4: score stays 0.882542 (p0022). tag: analytic-gradient projected ascent on r (hard max, full n)
claim: Exact-R analytic-gradient projected ascent using the true argmax for the max (not a softmax), at full N=200000 with backtracking line search and step resets, gains nothing over the binomial start (0.882542 unchanged). This shows the earlier softmax L-BFGS stall was not an artifact of smoothing the max: the binomial construction is a genuine local maximum for whole-plateau gradient moves too.

tag: inverse design via deconvolution toward a trapezoid target

tag: global gaussian smoothing of log-heights (coherent deformati
claim: Convolving log h of the 0.882542 binomial with a Gaussian kernel over a range of widths and amplitudes, then refining, leaves the score exactly unchanged at 0.882542 (p0042). Coherent smoothing of the singular endpoint does not shorten the post-plateau tail enough to beat the start — consistent with the binomial being a rigid stationary point for smooth global deformations.

Joint coordinate descent on a 6-mode cosine envelope added to log h of the binomial, allowing simultaneous multi-mode reshaping (not one mode at a time), leaves the score at 0.882542 (p0043). Even coherent multi-mode interior envelopes cannot improve on the binomial, strengthening the picture that the remaining loss is locked in the tail and not reachable by smooth global modulation.
